features.label: libwebrtc integration

patches.author: Philipp Hancke
patches.subject: implement webrtc rtxSsrc and retransmission stats

patches.author: az
patches.subject: Keep hardware H.264 decode for WebRTC when no software decoder is available.

patches.author: Philipp Hancke
patches.subject: don't send DTMF on a disabled sender

features.summary: Recent changes to the Firefox browser's integration with **WebRTC**, the technology enabling real-time communication like video calls, have focused on improving video quality and resource management. The integration now includes support for **RTX (Retransmission) SSRC** (Synchronization Source identifiers) and retransmission stats, which help manage video streams more effectively, particularly in challenging network conditions. Firefox will also continue using hardware acceleration for decoding H.264 video, ensuring smoother performance when a software decoder isn't available. Additionally, the browser will avoid sending Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF) signals—the tones used for phone keypad input—from disabled video feeds, further enhancing the clarity and efficiency of communication. These updates contribute to more reliable and efficient video calling experiences for users.

features.label: Connection transport (ICE / DTLS)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Move RTCIceCandidate out of JSImpl.

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Some type/const correctness fixes in nICEr.

features.summary: Recent changes to the connection transport in Firefox focus on improving the handling of WebRTC, the technology behind video calls. By moving `RTCIceCandidate`, a crucial component used for establishing web connections, out of the JavaScript implementation, the browser can now manage these connection attempts more efficiently. Additionally, implementing type and constant correctness fixes in the nICEr library enhances the reliability and performance of ICE (Interactive Connectivity Establishment), which helps ensure better connectivity in challenging network conditions. These updates ultimately contribute to a more robust and seamless real-time communication experience for users.

features.label: WebRTC web API (RTCPeerConnection)

patches.author: Byron Campen
patches.subject: Implement RTCIceTransport selected candidate pair API.

patches.author: Nicolas Grunbaum
patches.subject: report outbound-rtp stats in stable;r=dbaker,bwc

features.summary: Recent updates to the WebRTC web API significantly enhance how developers can manage network connections for real-time communication. The implementation of the **RTCIceTransport selected candidate pair API** allows for improved monitoring and control over which network candidates are being used during a peer connection, which can lead to better performance in video calls and other interactive applications. Additionally, by enabling the reporting of outbound RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol) statistics, developers can now gain insights into data being sent across the connection, facilitating more effective troubleshooting and optimization. This is crucial for maintaining high-quality connections in applications relying on WebRTC, such as video conferencing tools.

features.label: WebRTC

features.summary: Recent updates to the negotiation engine in Firefox have refined its handling of Real-Time Transport Protocol (RTP) tasks. Notably, RTP header extensions are now managed using a more efficient format, which enhances how data is handled during video and audio streaming. Additionally, the engine will now filter out redundant remote entries that conflict with our sending SSRCs (Synchronization Source Identifiers), optimizing media interactions. **These changes improve overall performance and reliability in multimedia communication, such as video calls, by ensuring that only unique and relevant data is processed**. Lastly, the Opus codec parameters like ptime, minptime, and maxptime are now properly parsed and utilized, which helps in optimizing audio quality and performance in different network conditions.
